record.original_question: Let d be an integer that is not divisible√by n-th powers of primes, let xn − d be an irreducible polynomial over Q, let θ = n d, and let K = Q(θ) be the radical extension of degree n of the field Q. The multiplicative group K ∗ of the field K is canonically embedded into the group AutQ(K) of all invertible Q-linear mappings of the Q-space K; let T be the image of K ∗ under this embedding. In the natural basis 1, θ, θ2,..., θn−1 of the Q-space K the group AutQ(K) corresponds to G = GL(n, Q), and the subgroup T to a subgroup T(d) (unsplit maximal torus). Every subgroup H of G containing T(d) and some one-dimensional transformation is rich in elementary transvections(V. A. Koibaev, St. Petersbg. Math. J., 21, no. 5(2010), 731–742) and thus defines a net σ = σ(H) (V. A. Koibaev, A. V. Shilov, J. Math. Sci. New York 171, no. 3(2010), 380–385). Let E(σ) denote the subgroup generated by all transvections in the net group G(σ). Is it true that H ⩽ NG(E(σ))? This inclusion was proved in the case n = 2(V. A. Koibaev, Dokl. Math., 41, no. 3(1990), 414–416).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer and let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ be such that $d$ is not divisible by the $n$-th power of any prime and the polynomial $x^n - d$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$. Set $\theta = \sqrt[n]{d}$ and let $K = \mathbb{Q}(\theta)$, the radical extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ of degree $n$. The multiplicative group $K^*$ embeds canonically into $\operatorname{Aut}_\mathbb{Q}(K)$, the group of all invertible $\mathbb{Q}$-linear maps of $K$, by sending $a \in K^*$ to multiplication-by-$a$; let $T \subset \operatorname{Aut}_\mathbb{Q}(K)$ denote the image. With respect to the basis $1, \theta, \theta^2, \ldots, \theta^{n-1}$ of the $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $K$, identify $\operatorname{Aut}_\mathbb{Q}(K)$ with $G = \operatorname{GL}(n, \mathbb{Q})$, and let $T(d) \subset G$ be the subgroup corresponding to $T$ (an unsplit maximal torus). 

A net (carpet) over $\mathbb{Q}$ is a family $\sigma = (\sigma_{ij})_{1 \leq i, j \leq n}$ of additive subgroups of $\mathbb{Q}$ satisfying $\sigma_{ir}\sigma_{rj} \subseteq \sigma_{ij}$ for all $i, r, j$. The net group $G(\sigma)$ is the subgroup of $G$ consisting of matrices $g = (g_{ij})$ with $g_{ij} \in \sigma_{ij}$ for $i \neq j$ (and diagonal entries invertible), and $E(\sigma)$ is the subgroup of $G(\sigma)$ generated by all elementary transvections $t_{ij}(\xi) = e + \xi e_{ij}$ with $\xi \in \sigma_{ij}$, $i \neq j$.

Now let $H$ be any subgroup of $G$ containing $T(d)$ together with at least one one-dimensional transformation (a transvection or a one-dimensional dilation). It is known that such $H$ is rich in elementary transvections, and so it determines a net $\sigma = \sigma(H)$.

Question: Is it true that $H \leq N_G(E(\sigma))$, i.e., every such $H$ normalizes the elementary net subgroup $E(\sigma(H))$?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Koibaev and collaborators (Journal of Mathematical Sciences, 2015) computes the normalizer $N_G(E(\sigma))$ of the elementary net group associated with a nonsplit maximal torus $T(d)$ in $\operatorname{GL}(n,k)$ over a field of odd characteristic, and there are related results on overgroups of nonsplit tori. However, available sources do not explicitly confirm that the inclusion $H \leq N_G(E(\sigma(H)))$ has been established for arbitrary $n$ in the setting stated; the case $n=2$ is known. The current status thus appears unresolved or unverifiable from public sources.

status_evidence.title: The Normalizer of the Elementary Net Group Associated with a Nonsplit Torus in the General Linear Group Over a Field
status_evidence.snippet: The normalizer N(σ) of the elementary net group E(σ) associated with a nonsplit maximal torus T(d) in GL(n,k) over a field k of odd characteristic is computed.
status_evidence.claim: Related work computes the normalizer of E(σ) for nonsplit tori, but does not directly state that every overgroup H of T(d) lies in N_G(E(σ(H))).

status_evidence.title: The subgroups of the group gl(2,k) that contain a nonsplit maximal torus
status_evidence.snippet: Koibaev's earlier work treats the n=2 case of overgroups of nonsplit maximal tori.
status_evidence.claim: The case n=2 of the inclusion has been settled in earlier work.
